method: Independent confirm pass: every listed component judged against the current LaTeX on the recursive input route (body entry, declared annex proof and any further on-route treatment cited in evidence) and against the held source at the cited locators; source items compared are the source's presentation of the same definition, theorem or example, its stated hypotheses, equivalent forms, cases and attached claims. Correctness was not assessed.

components.gap: Durrett (p. 17) defines an extended random variable as a map from a measurable domain D in F into [-infinity, infinity] carrying the Borel sets of its usual topology, generated by intervals [-infinity, a), (a, b) and (b, infinity]. The entry requires maps defined on all of Omega (def:p15-measurable-map: all functions are defined on all of Omega) and uses the sigma-algebra generated by the sets [-infinity, a], without recording the source's partial-domain variant and without showing that the two sigma-algebras on the extended line coincide. The source variant is narrowed without declaration.

components.gap: Durrett's Theorem A.1.5 (app. A.1, pp. 457-458) proves that two measures, defined on sigma-fields containing sigma(P), that agree on a pi-system P containing sets A_n increasing to Omega with finite measure, agree on sigma(P). The entry states uniqueness only for probability measures, and the route's sigma-finite uniqueness (thm:p15-premeasure-extension) requires agreement on an algebra. The source's general pi-system uniqueness theorem for sigma-finite measures is not supplied. Durrett also attributes the pi-lambda theorem to Dynkin ('Dynkin's pi-lambda theorem', p. 456); that attribution is not recorded for this theorem on the route (later annexes only use the phrase 'Dynkin system').
